name: core
notes: core block attribute portability (core data-boundary exact-image audit): WordPress 7.0.3's registered core block schemas were enumerated from WP_Block_Type_Registry rather than inferred from attribute names. The declared media ids (audio, cover, file, image, media-text, video), page-list ids, reusable/navigation ids, and avatar userId now cross environments through the post ledger or an exact user:<login> token; scalar/list zero is WordPress's unset convention and normalizes to absence without a dangling warning. Every registered core URL/href/src/poster field, page-list-item.link, and every string leaf of video.tracks routes through tokenize:text, because parse_blocks() exposes comment JSON separately from innerHTML and the generic body tokenizer cannot see those bytes. core/file.fileId is explicitly lint_ok: its registered schema sources the DOM element id attribute and WordPress never resolves it as an entity id. sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_data_boundary.sh binds the inventory and round-trip to the exact WordPress image and exercises divergent post, attachment, page, and user ids. core/legacy-widget is deliberately not papered over: its id points into the widget-instance ledger and its alternate instance.hash is salted per environment; all three attributes carry explicit unsupported dispositions, so either real form refuses before publication until a generic codec can rebind the ledger form and re-sign embedded settings with verified target behavior.

core assumption-surface audit for WordPress 7.1 (DUO platform-71, source-level, no live run): 7.1 is the current release and the shipped claim now names it, so every 7.0.3-grounded declaration above was re-checked against 7.1's own source (wordpress-7.1.zip, sha256 d1ae02b5ae18428031ffc3943659fa87ab361d827f4aa804adf9276e4dc75df6, diffed file-by-file against wordpress-7.0.3.zip) rather than re-asserted. ONE declaration changed and it is above: 7.1 adds six core blocks (playlist, playlist-track, tabs, tab-list, tab-panel, tab-panels) and exactly one of them carries reference-shaped attributes. core/playlist-track.id is a REQUIRED attachment id -- render_block_core_playlist_track() returns '' for an empty one (wp-includes/blocks/playlist-track.php:20-22, @since 7.1.0) -- so it is declared kind: post like every other core media id; .src is the media URL and .image is an absolute artwork URL esc_url()'d into an at playlist-track.php:39, and both are declared tokenize: text for the same reason every other core block URL is: parse_blocks() exposes comment JSON separately from innerHTML and the generic body tokenizer cannot see those bytes. Undeclared, .id alone would have been loud (BlockReferenceScanner::scan() raises unregistered_block_attr for id-shaped attrs, agent/src/Review/BlockReferenceScanner.php:60-68) while .src and .image would have published the SOURCE environment's absolute media URLs onto the target in silence -- which is why the claim could not widen to 7.1 without this row. core/playlist itself declares nothing: its attributes are colors, booleans, an enum and a caption. The tabs family declares nothing either: tab-list.tabs is an array sourced by query from button elements whose item shape is exactly {label: rich-text} (no entity id), tab-panel.label is a plain string, and tabs' own activeTabIndex/editorActiveTabIndex are positional integers, not entity references. core/playlist-track.blob is DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED, recorded here rather than left silent: its block.json marks it role: "local", i.e. an editor-session Blob URL that resolves in no environment including the one that minted it, so carrying it would be copying a dangling handle -- the same shape of written exclusion as img_caption_shortcode's id below. VERIFIED UNCHANGED between 7.0.3 and 7.1, so this is a review rather than an assumption: wp-admin/includes/schema.php is byte-identical (every fresh-install option seed, the permalink_structure default and populate_roles all unchanged, which is what the options.* and wp_user_roles notes below rest on); wp_create_initial_post_meta() is byte-identical (wp_pattern_sync_status unchanged); gallery_shortcode() differs only in docblock text, so the four reference-shaped shortcode atts declared above are unchanged; class-wp-embed.php is byte-identical (the _oembed_ post-meta cache boundary below is unchanged); get_user_count()/wp_update_user_counts() are unchanged; WP_Roles::_init()'s computed option name is unchanged (class-wp-roles.php differs only in an add_role() return-type normalization); $wp_db_version is 61833 in both, so no schema upgrade separates the two; and the block parser differs only by count($stack)-1 becoming array_key_last($stack) (class-wp-block-parser.php:345), which is why sandbox/tests/support/wp-block-parser-stub.php stays valid for the offline corpus. One 7.1 addition was found and is OUT OF THIS MANIFEST'S SCOPE, recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it: wp_insert_user() seeds a new 'infinite_scrolling' USER meta key (wp-includes/user.php) -- core.json declares no user_meta surface at all, so there is nothing here for it to change. The 7.1 half of this audit is source-level only at the time of writing; sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_data_boundary.sh's per-series inventory table is what turns it into live evidence.

core oEmbed post-meta cache boundary (core data-boundary exact-image audit): rendering the real core/embed catalog through WordPress 7.0.3 generated an `_oembed_<32-lowercase-hex>={{unknown}}` row on the divergent target even though the source had no cache row, and the second capture correctly stopped on that previously-unclassified key before this declaration. WP_Embed::shortcode() derives `_oembed_<md5(url . serialize(attrs))>` and `_oembed_time_<same-md5>`, writes fetched HTML or the `{{unknown}}` failure sentinel plus an optional fetch timestamp, and delete_oembed_caches() invalidates the whole `_oembed_` post-meta family; these are lazy derived render caches, never authored state. The declaration is deliberately the anchored lowercase 32-hex pair, not WordPress's broad deletion prefix, so `_oembed_custom` and malformed/extended lookalikes remain loud. It uses post_meta_patterns rather than legacy meta_patterns because the latter also classifies wp_termmeta: evidence proves this family only on posts, and an identically named term-meta value must not disappear by inference.

DUO-3509 fresh-process correction (live core conformance, exact candidate 7aeb89cea74dd77c7b8f9cecdd7720c43484b004): the permalink note below describes the first offline-green implementation when it says the loaded runtime is reinitialized; that sentence is superseded by this evidence. A real dirty target proved WP_Rewrite::init() late in apply retained category/tag permastructs registered under the old front while clearing other registration buckets; its immediate receipt and post routes looked green but a fresh process generated different ordered rules. NativeActions now launches one fixed engine-owned `wp eval` child (no manifest-controlled command or argument) which boots WordPress after the authored row commits, performs `flush_rules(false)`, compares WordPress's sanitized persistence projection with a checked raw database read, separately compares the generated rules with the effective option-filtered runtime, and returns only a closed hash/count/type envelope. The two projections may differ intentionally: Yoast SEO 28.3 removes its dynamic sitemap routes through sanitize_option_rewrite_rules before persistence and adds them back through option_rewrite_rules on read, so requiring raw/effective byte equality made an incomplete apply unrecoverable whenever core's retry action ran with Yoast active. Pretty permalinks produce an ordered rules array; WordPress 7.0.3 deliberately persists the exact empty string for a plain or absent permalink structure, because WP_Rewrite::refresh_rewrite_rules() initializes the property to that sentinel and rewrite_rules() returns early without assigning its empty array. The parent validates the exact type as well as the hash/count and independently re-reads both durable and effective projections; arbitrary child stderr is never reflected, and any warning is a refusal. This is the same necessary process boundary as post-apply canonical verification: replaying `init` hooks would duplicate arbitrary plugin side effects, while hand-reconstructing post-type/taxonomy/plugin registrations would silently guess at extension semantics. An absent permalink row still stays absent because the child writes only rewrite_rules. The live gates exercise both native representations, category/tag front changes, Yoast-style dynamic sanitization/readback, public HTTP routing, a filtered write veto, exact retry, and zero-change idempotence.

options.active_plugins/template/stylesheet (task #39, docs/code-half.md §3.1): the cross-partition invariant DESIGN.md §3.4 names (active_plugins ⊆ plugins in code/) needs these captured, but applying them via direct SQL is actively wrong — activate_plugin()/switch_theme() do real one-time setup in register_activation_hook/switch_theme/after_switch_theme that a raw UPDATE wp_options would skip while leaving WordPress believing the plugin/theme is active. Classified managed (the same class _menu_item_* and _wp_attached_file already use for 'authored-domain fact, bespoke capture/apply handling'): Capture::build_options() reads them with bespoke code alongside (not through) the authored-options whitelist loop; Apply::apply_options() excludes them from the generic direct-SQL upsert loop; only agent/src/Promotion/Deploy.php's `wp duo deploy` reconciles them, via real WP APIs, deliberately outside Canary::arm()/disarm() — activation hooks must fire there, and apply's canary requires the opposite. Values are plain portable strings (plugin file paths, theme directory slugs) — no ref-tokenization, since that stability across environments IS the invariant.

post_meta.wp_pattern_sync_status (task #31): Site-Editor-only flag on wp_block posts, verified empirically on a running install (e1, WP core 7.0.2, wp-includes/post.php's wp_create_initial_post_meta() — no plugin involved, registered unconditionally regardless of active theme). register_post_meta('wp_block', 'wp_pattern_sync_status', ['type'=>'string','single'=>true,'sanitize_callback'=>'sanitize_text_field','show_in_rest'=>['schema'=>['type'=>'string','enum'=>['partial','unsynced']]]]). Confirmed by direct DB read: a fresh wp_block post carries ZERO postmeta rows at all — the default 'fully synced' pattern state is the KEY'S ABSENCE, not a value like 'full'/'synced' (there is no such value in the enum). Once set, the value is a plain, non-serialized scalar string ('unsynced' or 'partial') sitting directly in wp_postmeta.meta_value — confirmed both via direct meta (`wp post meta update`) and via the REST route (WP_REST_Blocks_Controller::filter_response_by_context() promotes meta.wp_pattern_sync_status to a top-level response property and strips it from the meta sub-object on READ, but WRITES still go through the ordinary meta sub-object — verified empirically with an authenticated rest_do_request() POST carrying {"meta":{"wp_pattern_sync_status":"partial"}}, which persisted to the same postmeta row read back via get_post_meta()). Classified authored, plain (no ref — it's a flag, not an id) — the existing generic no-ref post_meta path (tokenize_text() on a scalar string, a no-op here since 'unsynced'/'partial' contain no env-bound substring) already round-trips it correctly with zero new engine code, exactly like _wp_page_template.

shortcode_attrs.gallery (DUO-3259): the LEGACY [gallery ...] SHORTCODE's four genuine reference-shaped attributes, grounded via direct read of WordPress 7.0.2's real wp-includes/media.php gallery_shortcode() source, not assumed — distinct from (and complementary to, not redundant with) block_attrs['core/gallery']'s own 'ids' entry above, which covers the separate GUTENBERG BLOCK's own JSON-attribute schema; one is raw shortcode text sitting in post_content, the other a parsed block attribute, two different WordPress mechanisms that happen to share a display name. 'id' defaults to the CURRENT post when the attribute is absent (used as post_parent for get_children() once include/exclude are unset) — an implicit self-reference needing no rewrite at all, since it resolves correctly against the same post's own regenerated id after apply for free; an omitted 'id' is therefore never flagged by lint or the unscoped-ref gate, only a LITERAL numeric 'id="N"' is rewritten. 'ids' is aliased verbatim into 'include' when non-empty (`$attr['include'] = $attr['ids'];`, read directly in gallery_shortcode()) — both share the exact same comma-separated-post-id format 'include' and 'exclude' also use, fed straight to get_posts()/get_children(). img_caption_shortcode()'s own 'id' attribute (the [caption id="..."] shape DUO-3259 was originally filed assuming needed an equivalent codec) is DELIBERATELY NOT declared here: confirmed by reading img_caption_shortcode() directly, that attribute is sanitize_html_class()'d and emitted verbatim as a DOM id for CSS/JS targeting only — never parsed back into a numeric attachment reference anywhere in WordPress core. There is nothing to codec; 'caption' is ruled explicitly unsupported for that reason (no reference-shaped attribute exists to declare), not because a codec for it would be hard to build.

menu_fields.locations (DUO-3272): the v0 baseline for every menu's location assignment — captured from the active theme's raw theme_mods_<stylesheet>['nav_menu_locations'] (Capture::scope_menus()), applied via a direct Db::update/insert write (Apply::assign_locations(), deliberately hook-free like every other product-database mutation). This is the ordinary, correct behavior for every site with no plugin managing per-language menu state. A pinned plugin manifest may reclassify this field 'derived' when it can prove the raw slot is actually a mutable projection THAT plugin's own machinery rewrites at will (Polylang: see manifests/polylang.json's own note, and Policy::menu_field_class()'s docblock, and the DUO-3272 issue for the full empirical grounding) — Policy::active_menu_field_reclassifications() surfaces any such override as a loud plan warning, the same DUO-3249 precedence and transparency mechanism options.default_category already uses.

dynamic_options.theme_mods (DUO-3264, owner ruling issue comment 9fd882a6 — pass 1 of a two-pass split, DUO-3278 carries pass 2, widgets/sidebars): before this, ONLY the nav_menu_locations key inside theme_mods_<stylesheet> was ever read or written (Capture.php/Apply.php's own bespoke, hand-rolled code, task/DUO-3272) — every other key a theme puts in that blob was neither captured nor gated, simply invisible. Grounded empirically against a real classic theme (Twenty Twenty-One) and a real FSE/block theme (Twenty Twenty-Five), using WordPress's own Customizer-equivalent APIs (set_theme_mod(), wp_update_custom_css_post(), add_theme_support('custom-header')), not assumed: 'background_color' is a plain authored scalar. 'custom_logo' is a plain int attachment id, ref:post. 'header_image' is a full absolute URL string (NOT an attachment id) — needs no ref/json_refs at all: Capture::capture_value()'s own plain-string fallback already runs tokenize_text() on any authored option value with neither declared, the same {{home}}/{{uploads}} rewriting block content gets. 'header_image_data' is a nested PLAIN ARRAY (confirmed by reading wp-includes/class-wp-customize-manager.php's own Customizer save-path directly — `header_image` setting saves build `array('attachment_id'=>...,'url'=>...,'thumbnail_url'=>...,...)`; an earlier live test that used a PHP object instead was this session's own test-code artifact, not real WordPress behavior, caught by Capture::assert_plain() correctly refusing it) mixing a real ref (attachment_id) with two more URLs (url/thumbnail_url) and plain ints (height/width) — also needs no new grammar: Tokens::struct_capture() already calls tokenize_leaves() unconditionally on the WHOLE structure after applying the declared json_refs path, so the URL leaves tokenize for free once attachment_id's own path is declared. 'custom_css_post_id' looked like it might need new machinery but does not: it is a plain int pointing to a REAL post of post_type custom_css whose post_content IS the authored CSS (post_name is literally the stylesheet slug) — an ordinary post-scope addition (a site's own policy.post_types), not a theme_mods content problem; the pointer key itself is ref:post like any other. 'sidebars_widgets' and 'wp_classic_sidebars', found NESTED INSIDE theme_mods (distinct from the top-level sidebars_widgets option of the same name) are WordPress's own theme-switch migration bookkeeping — confirmed live: switching Twenty Twenty-One to Twenty Twenty-Five auto-populated both, a timestamped snapshot of the PREVIOUS theme's widget layout kept so nothing is lost if the admin switches back. Classified runtime: env-local residue, never portable authored content, the same treatment core.json's own rewrite_rules/cron already get.

dynamic_options' own resolution mechanism (DUO-3264, fork A): theme_mods_<stylesheet>'s option NAME is computed, not fixed, so it cannot use the ordinary sub_keys grammar directly (which assumes an exactly-known name, e.g. this same manifest's own future consumers or polylang.json's/yoast.json's already-shipped 'polylang'/'wpseo'). Unlike an ordinary option_patterns match (every matching row is simultaneously live and relevant, e.g. every _transient_* row), only ONE theme_mods_* row is ever the current site's own authored state — the active theme's. A theme_mods_<some other theme> row is stale residue from a theme that used to be active, the identical shape of problem as the wp_classic_sidebars/nested-sidebars_widgets residue above, just one level up (a whole ROW instead of two KEYS within it). Policy::dynamic_options()/resolve_dynamic_option()/is_dynamic_option_residue() give this its own small, reusable primitive (prefix + a named resolver, 'active_stylesheet' the one proven case) instead of a second bespoke hand-rolled path beside nav_menu_locations's own — see Policy.php's own docblocks for the full mechanism. Every OTHER theme_mods_* row is never discovered by any capture/pending path at all (this mechanism is its own dedicated enumeration, independent of option_namespaces/gate_scan(), matching sub_keyed_options()'s own established independence) — never unclassified-pending, never captured, exactly as the ruling requires, with zero risk of the capture-blocking regression a namespace-based approach would have introduced (verified live before ruling that out, not assumed — see the DUO-3264 issue's own comment thread). Removed this manifest's own long-standing `option_patterns` entry `{class:special_theme_mods, match:^theme_mods_}` as part of this same change — it had zero consumers anywhere in the engine (grep-confirmed before removal) and, once dynamic_options started producing real theme_mods_<stylesheet> document records, would have silently WON the ordinary single-name lookup ahead of this mechanism's own fallback, masking every sub_keys rule below with an inert class no code has ever handled — caught live, not by inspection alone, when a capture's own repository-authorization pass refused a freshly-captured tree citing exactly that stale class name.

top-level sidebars_widgets + widget_<type> — the FULL evolution, walk-back included, because the correction is the valuable record here, not a clean-looking history (DUO-3264, three owner premises in sequence, each corrected by the next piece of live evidence): (1) the split ruling assumed these were already LOUD (unclassified -> pending gate) and required this pass to leave that untouched. Empirically false — core.json had never declared an option_namespaces entry for either, so Pending::scan()/gate_scan() never saw these names at all; confirmed live, reported before the next step. (2) Corrected ruling: declare option_namespaces for ^sidebars_widgets$/^widget_, explicitly classify the ~18 core-registered widget_<type> names (WordPress's own wp_widgets_init(), verified directly against wp-includes/widgets.php in the exact image this project's sandbox uses — WP_Widget_Links/widget_links is the only conditionally-registered default, gated behind link_manager_enabled, off by default, correctly excluded) plus sidebars_widgets itself `runtime`, by exact name never a `^widget_` pattern — believed at the time to be the universal blocking net for any undeclared type with real content. (3) DUO-3278 (widget portability, uuid ledger identity) merged concurrently and, on actually reading SidebarState.php's own logic rather than only its diff, its load_widget_options() already has an unconditional, independent, EARLIER-firing guard for the identical condition (any widget_<type> row with real instances and an undeclared type refuses capture outright) — running before build_options() even gets a chance, making the namespace declaration above provably unreachable dead weight for the widget_* family, and — since it matched on mere NAMESPACE PRESENCE rather than SidebarState's own real-content qualification — stricter than intended besides (would have blocked on an empty, never-populated third-party widget type the moment its owning plugin activates, not just when someone actually places an instance). Reverted: no option_namespaces entry, no per-name options.widget_*/sidebars_widgets classification. What remains true and load-bearing: SidebarState::load_widget_options()'s own guard is the actual, sufficient, already-shipped blocking net for the whole widget_<type> family (both DUO-3278's 3 covered types and every other core/third-party one) — see SidebarState.php's own docblock at that guard for its message and remedies. Empty, auto-registered widget_<type> rows (every core type on a fresh install, before any instance is placed) remain UNSCANNED by design at zero code cost on either side of this walk-back: contentless scaffolding was never captured before this issue, is not captured now, and any REAL content triggers SidebarState's own declared-or-refuse guard regardless. This note itself, not a namespace declaration, is what makes that a recorded decision rather than a silent omission. (4) One more finding while verifying (3) live, filed as its own closed record since it names a completeness gap in SidebarState's own guard rather than anything this manifest declares: that guard's own refusal message advertised a 'classify it runtime' remedy that did not function (the guard never consulted options.* classifications, only widgets{}) — fixed at the source, not here; see DUO-3283 and SidebarState::load_widget_options()'s own docblock.

options.permalink_structure / options.blog_public (DUO-3509): the two Settings-screen values a fresh `duo init` on WP 7.0.3 demanded a decision for and core.json had never declared, classified against WordPress 7.0.3's own source rather than from memory. permalink_structure is the site's URL grammar — a plain portable structure string (install's own default is '/%year%/%monthnum%/%day%/%postname%/', wp-admin/includes/schema.php:576; '' means plain permalinks, schema.php:443), authored through Settings -> Permalinks (wp-admin/options-permalink.php:104-121) and sanitized as a structure, never as an id (wp-includes/formatting.php:5062). Authored, no ref, and no lint_ok needed — the value carries no numeric leaf for Pending::numeric_candidates() to mistake for a reference. rewrite_rules below is `derived`, and WordPress rebuilds it ONLY when WP_Rewrite::refresh_rewrite_rules() runs; WP_Rewrite::wp_rewrite_rules() otherwise accepts any non-empty stored array. Nothing in core hooks a raw permalink_structure write: update_home_siteurl() flushes for home/siteurl only, and wp-admin/options-permalink.php flushes because that screen explicitly calls the native API. Apply writes options through hook-free direct SQL, so the manifest now selects the engine-owned `rewrite.flush` action on the exact `option:permalink_structure` surface. NativeActions uses the fresh-process correction above, requires wp_loaded so no mutation can be deferred beyond the receipt, performs `flush_rules(false)` so target-owned .htaccess/web.config bytes are never touched, and verifies the persisted native representation against a fresh WP_Rewrite read: ordered array for pretty permalinks, exact empty string for plain or absent. Its receipt contains hashes/counts/types only because extension-contributed rules can contain site paths. An explicit permalink_structure tombstone is preserved as absence by supplying WordPress's semantic empty-string default only during init; no action recreates the authored row. The declared effects enumerate the rewrite_rules checkpoint, external option cache, and every WordPress 7.0.3 option/rewrite filter or hook this path can invoke, so rollback planning does not pretend the core call is database-only. blog_public is Settings -> Reading's 'Discourage search engines' flag: the string '1'/'0' (schema default '1', schema.php:474; its own sanitize_option() case at formatting.php:4939; written by install at wp-admin/includes/upgrade.php:84 and by the ordinary allowed-options save, wp-admin/options.php:149). Authored — a human sets it and it means the same thing on any host. `lint_ok: true` is REQUIRED here, not decorative: '1' is a numeric scalar, so Lint's shallow bare_id scan (Lint.php:575 via Pending::resolve_id()) would otherwise resolve it to post 1 — 'Hello world!' on every fresh install — and report a false unrewritten reference on every capture. Recorded trade-off: a team that wants staging noindexed while production is indexed does NOT get that from this classification, because apply carries the source's value; the remedy is the ordinary site-level override (`wp duo classify options blog_public env`, Policy::set_rule() writing site.duo.json, which outranks every manifest in PolicyRuleResolver::details()) — the same escape hatch that makes permalink_structure env-bound for a team whose environments deliberately differ.

options.fresh_site / theme_switched / current_theme / uninstall_plugins / user_count (DUO-3509): five WordPress-written rows the same fresh `duo init` surfaced as unclassified. All five are excluded, each for its own verified reason (WordPress 7.0.3 source, read directly). fresh_site — install sets it to 1 (wp-admin/includes/upgrade.php:87) and _delete_option_fresh_site() flips it to '0' the first time THIS install publishes (wp-includes/functions.php:4762); it gates the Customizer's first-run branch (class-wp-customize-manager.php:604) and the HTTPS-migration decision (https-migration.php:139). Per-install lifecycle state, recomputable from nothing Duo captures, and carrying a source's '0' onto a genuinely fresh target would silently suppress that target's own first-run behavior. theme_switched — switch_theme() writes the OUTGOING stylesheet (wp-includes/theme.php:840) purely so check_theme_switched() can consume it on the very next page load and immediately clear it back to false (theme.php:3475, :3510): a one-shot self-consuming baton between two requests of one environment. current_theme — switch_theme() writes the new theme's display Name (theme.php:815, `$new_theme->get('Name')`), and it is read in exactly two places, both legacy `mods_{name}` migration lookups that fall back to wp_get_theme()->get('Name') without ever repairing the row (get_theme_mods() theme.php:1031, remove_theme_mods() theme.php:1166). Classified runtime rather than derived DELIBERATELY, and the reasoning matters because for options the two are engine-identical (only `authored` is captured — OptionsCapture.php:104/150/243 — and only `authored` is written by apply): `derived` in this manifest means a row something actually rebuilds, as rewrite_rules is rebuilt whenever it is empty. Nothing rebuilds current_theme — a direct `wp option update stylesheet` leaves it naming the old theme forever, because only switch_theme(), a lifecycle MUTATION rather than a repair, ever writes it. A row nobody repairs is env-local residue, which is exactly what runtime means here. Duo needs no declaration for it in any case: the only path that changes a managed site's active theme is agent/src/Promotion/Deploy.php's real switch_theme() call for the `managed` template/stylesheet pair (see this manifest's own active_plugins note), and that call writes current_theme itself. uninstall_plugins — a plugin-file => uninstall-callback map that register_uninstall_hook() maintains at activation time (wp-includes/plugin.php:944-950) and uninstall_plugin() prunes (wp-admin/includes/plugin.php:1283-1335). Its content is a function of which plugins THIS environment activated — the same activation lifecycle active_plugins is `managed` for — so carrying it as data would record uninstall callbacks for a code partition the target may not even have. Runtime, the class recently_activated already carries for the same lifecycle reason. user_count — wp_update_user_counts() caches `SELECT COUNT(ID) FROM $wpdb->users` (wp-includes/user.php:1517-1538; on a single site update_network_option() falls through to the ordinary wp_options row), refreshed by the twicedaily `wp_update_user_counts` cron event (wp_schedule_update_user_counts()) and by wp_maybe_update_user_counts() on user create/delete. It IS regenerable — but from wp_users, which DESIGN.md 3.1 keeps deliberately environment-local ('users remain environment-local non-entities'), so the fact it caches is the TARGET's own headcount and a captured value would be a foreign environment's. Runtime for that reason, not for want of a rebuilder.

options.wp_user_roles is DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED (DUO-3509) — this note is the deliverable, because a wrong `authored` here would copy one environment's whole capability map over another's. Three findings from WordPress 7.0.3, each independently sufficient. (1) The NAME is not stable: WP_Roles::_init() computes it as `$wpdb->get_blog_prefix($this->site_id) . 'user_roles'` (wp-includes/class-wp-roles.php:342), so an exact `wp_user_roles` rule matches only sites left on the default `wp_` table prefix and would leave an `xy_user_roles` site exactly as unclassified as it is today — a declaration that reads as complete and is not. (2) The VALUE is a merge, not authored configuration: populate_roles() seeds it at install (wp-admin/includes/schema.php:719+) and every plugin activation then mutates it in place through WP_Roles::add_role()/add_cap(), each of which update_option()s the whole map (class-wp-roles.php:190/214/239/258); WooCommerce 11.0.1's installer alone adds the customer and shop_manager roles and grants its own caps to administrator and shop_manager (WC_Install::create_roles(), includes/class-wc-install.php:2262+). The live value is therefore core defaults plus whatever the plugins THIS environment has active have added, at THEIR installed versions. (3) There is NO safe apply path. Duo writes options by hook-free direct SQL, so `authored` would replace the target's entire roles map with the source's — granting caps for plugins the target does not have, and revoking caps a plugin on the target added at its own activation, with no lifecycle call (populate_roles(), a plugin activation hook) that would ever put them back. The `managed` escape used for active_plugins/template/stylesheet is unavailable for the same reason it works there: that class exists because Deploy.php can reconcile those three through real WordPress APIs, and no equivalent API reconciles a merged capability map. Genuine authored role customization is real but not expressible here, so the honest outcome is the loud one this project's posture requires (DESIGN.md 2, 'loud, blocking, scoped ... 95% correct is negative value'): the row stays unclassified, `duo pending` keeps demanding a per-site decision, and an operator who knows their environments' plugin sets agree can take it deliberately with the site-level override (`wp duo classify options <prefix>_user_roles authored`), recorded in that one site's site.duo.json instead of asserted for every site by this manifest. Classifying it `env` or `runtime` here was rejected for the opposite reason: both are silent exclusions, so a site that really had authored a custom role would lose it from its branchable partition with nobody told.
